diagram_math_checks.justification: Alpha maps M^{coH} tensor H to M by n tensor h -> nh (step 1.1). Beta maps M to M^{coH} tensor H as (P tensor id_H) rho (step 1.2), where rho:M -> M tensor H and P:M -> M^{coH}, P(m)=sum m_0 S(m_1) by F3 and the local coinvariant-projection lemma. Thus beta(m)=sum P(m_0) tensor m_1; P acts on the M component and the antipode acts on its H coaction component. This uses the tensor map, without assuming individual Sweedler summands coinvariant.

The left-to-right arrow is alpha and right-to-left is beta. Therefore the left round trip is beta alpha=id_{M^{coH} tensor H}, from step 2.1 using rho(n)=n tensor 1_H and sum h_1 S(h_2) tensor h_3=1_H tensor h. The right round trip is alpha beta=id_M from step 1.3 using sum S(h_1)h_2=epsilon(h)1_H and the counit. Labels and text agree with these composition orders.

Step 2.2 proves alpha preserves the right action and right coaction; step 3.1 transfers both identities to its inverse beta. No inverse antipode or bijectivity assumption was added. The proof remains unchanged and logically independent of the illustration.
